2026金融AI智能体落地新标杆：中原银行与中信建投最新实践启示
2026年6月，中国金融AI智能体落地迎来两个标志性事件：中原银行外呼营销智能体斩获”2026中国AI智能体领航者”奖项，中信建投证券”信谛听”智数平台1.5版本正式上线并率先在核心业务场景切换至国产大模型。这两条消息看似独立，实则指向同一个趋势——金融AI智能体的竞争，正从”模型参数竞赛”转向”规模化交付能力”的比拼。
趋势：金融AI智能体进入”可信交付”时代
截至2026年6月，中国已有近800款大模型完成备案，53.5%的银行已上线大模型应用（来源：2026年银行业大模型应用调研报告）。但与2025年的”试点潮”不同，2026年金融机构关注的核心问题已从”模型够不够强”变成了”交付够不够可靠”。
如我们在 《金融行业AI智能体落地指南》 中分析的，金融场景对AI智能体的核心要求是零容错。无论是外呼营销中的合规话术控制，还是投研分析中的信息溯源，任何一次模型”幻觉”都可能导致实质性业务风险。中原银行与中信建投的最新实践，恰好从两个不同维度回应了这一核心诉求。
中原银行：双引擎架构破解外呼营销合规难题
中原银行作为资产规模超1.4万亿的省属法人银行，拥有600余家营业网点、1.8万余名员工。其与中关村科金联合申报的”外呼营销智能体”项目，在2026中国AI智能体领航者评选中从众多参评项目中脱颖而出。
该项目的核心创新在于”通用大模型+SOP流程”与”业务微调大模型”的双引擎架构：
SOP强约束 ：通过标准作业流程（SOP）约束对话路径，确保外呼全程在合规框架内运行，从架构层面杜绝大模型”幻觉”带来的话术风险
业务微调 ：基于中原银行真实业务语料进行监督微调，大幅增强模型在存款、理财、个贷等场景下的语义理解和意图识别能力
人机协同 ：智能体完成客户意向初筛，高价值线索无缝转接至人工坐席深度转化
这种架构设计的关键洞察在于：金融场景不需要”全能”的AI，而是需要”受控”的AI。SOP相当于给AI画了一条合规的跑道，让它在这个范围内发挥最大效率，而不是自由探索。
中信建投：从”能生成”到”能负责”的AI落地标准
中信建投”信谛听”1.5版本的升级，则展示了另一条路径：以专业数据为核心壁垒构建可信AI体系。
值得关注的是，”信谛听”1.5率先切换至国产大模型DeepSeek V4并完成核心场景验证。有报道称，中信建投信息技术部门相关负责人在公开活动中对国产大模型能力与成本优势表达了肯定（具体表述未经当事人核实）。
“信谛听”1.5的核心升级包括三项关键能力：
自适应纠错框架 ：让代码自己改Bug，大幅提升策略回测效率
DeepTiming搜索 ：首次整合中信建投7000余篇研报，拆解为超10万个可溯源知识原子，用户提问20秒内获得附带原文链接的精准回答
多智能体协同研究 ：支持分析师团队与AI协同完成研究报告撰写
其中”DeepTiming搜索”的设计思路尤其值得关注——用专业审核过的研报框定信息边界，让每条结论都可溯源。这恰好回应了行业对AI语料污染的普遍担忧：高质量专有数据正在成为金融机构构建AI可信体系的关键防线。
金融AI智能体选型的三个关键维度
结合上述案例与当前市场供给（来源：2026年企业级AI智能体选型指南综合梳理），金融机构在评估AI智能体平台时建议关注以下三个维度：
维度 核心问题 中原银行方案 中信建投方案 合规可控 如何防止AI”越界”？ SOP流程约束+话术合规检查 研报知识原子+溯源机制 数据壁垒 AI是否基于真实业务数据？ 业务微调大模型+真实语料 20TB机构级金融数据+脱敏研报 国产适配 能否满足信创和数据安全要求？ 私有化部署+国产大模型接入 切换至DeepSeek V4完成验证 对于计划引入AI智能体的长沙及中部地区金融机构和类金融企业，这三个维度可以作为选型评估的基础框架。重点不在于平台功能多全面，而在于能否在合规前提下实现稳定的业务价值。
长沙企业的启示：金融AI智能体落地的”三先”策略
中原银行与中信建投的实践验证了一个核心结论：金融AI智能体落地的关键不在于技术有多前沿，而在于能否在合规框架下产出稳定的业务价值。对于长沙及中部地区面临AI转型的企业，建议采取”三先”策略：
先框定场景 ：选择容忍度相对较高、边界清晰的业务场景（如外呼初筛、文档处理、报告辅助），而非一开始就挑战核心交易系统
先建立标准 ：明确AI输出的合规要求和验证机制，确保每条AI结论都可回溯、可审计
先验证价值 ：通过小范围试点（如一个网点、一个业务条线）验证ROI后再规模化推广，避免一步到位的风险
如我们在 《2026国产大模型本地化部署成本实测》 中测算的，当前国产大模型的部署成本已降至单项目5-20万元的区间。这意味着即便是预算有限的中部企业，也完全可以在不盲目追求大规模投入的前提下，找到适合自己的AI智能体切入点。
结语：从单点试验到规模化落地的关键一步
中原银行的获奖与中信建投的升级表明，2026年中国金融AI智能体正在完成从”单点试验”到”规模化落地”的关键跨越。对于长沙及中部地区的企业决策者来说，现在的问题不是”要不要用AI”，而是”如何用AI”。从合规框架出发，以业务数据为基础，在小场景中验证价值——这或许是当下务实的AI落地路径之一。

X 上的 Rohan Paul：“GPT-5.6 helped break Chrome’s defenses for a $250,000 Google bounty.
Xbow engineer Brendan Dolan-Gavitt ran OpenAI’s gpt-5.6-sol, against the browser’s source code over six days and $40,000 of compute
The agents searched code, tested hypotheses, and drafted the exploit stages, while Dolan-Gavitt and colleagues picked targets, supplied context, and decided which pieces to join.
Reconstructing the Codex logs, Xbow put the compute bill at roughly $40,000, a fraction of the prize, and well below the months of specialist labor such work once demanded.
The finished chain turned ordinary JavaScript in a Chrome tab into code running outside every sandbox, crossing two protective boundaries through three separate flaws.
Google reproduced the chain, confirmed all three bugs, shipped fixes, and awarded the first $250,000 full-chain Chrome reward under rules it set”

就在今晚，Gemini 4 Argon，终于全面开放了。
其实这玩意，10月1号就已经官宣过一次了，就在OpenAI开完DevDay的第二天。
但是那一次，基本上就是纯官宣，没啥人能用上，只给一个叫Fairwind的网络安全计划开放，基本都是政府、关键基础设施、安全公司啊这些做防守的人。
终于在憋了两周之后，Google选在今天官宣了。
这一个多月，基本上新的大模型就是轮番轰炸，我简单顺了一下节奏。
9月4号，GPT-6 Astra。
9月22号，Grok 4.7。
9月23号，Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6 Sol和Luna，一夜三连发。
9月30号，OpenAI DevDay，GPT-6.1 Sol。
10月1号，Gemini 4 Argon官宣。
10月13号，Meta的第一个前沿模型，Muse Wonder。
10月14号，Gemini 4 Argon全面开放。
基本上海外的几个巨头都到齐了，不过在模型层面，目前Anthropic还是无可争议的T0梯队，然后是OpenAI紧随其后，Meta和Google奋力追赶，Grok还在玩泥巴中。
我已经很久没有给Gemini付过费了，今晚又给他们贡献了100美刀，升级了一下Ultra会员，来体验一下Gemini 4 Argon。
最终几个小时体验下来，我个人觉得，还是很难冲击Claude Opus 5.5和GPT-6 Astra的地位。
一个一个说吧。
一. Google这大半年
在聊Argon之前，我觉得得先聊聊谷歌这大半年。
大家才能更加对这个模型的使命有一些理解。。。
时间拨回去年11月，Gemini 3 Pro发布，那个时候，它可以说是全世界最好的模型之一。
然后，谷歌就开始了一段非常魔幻的日子。
2月份发了个Gemini 3.1 Pro，然后在5月的I/O上，承诺一个月内发Gemini 3.5 Pro。
结果一拖再拖，说3.5 Pro的进度落后了好几个月，其中一个原因，是代码能力没达到内部目标，没办法，Anthropic和OpenAI给的压力太大了。
结果最后拖着拖着，内部直接砍掉了。。。
然后8月5号，谷歌AI这边，直接大换血。
哈萨比斯卸任Google DeepMind的CEO，改当DeepMind董事长兼Alphabet首席科学家，然后由科雷接手。
同一天，在谷歌干了27年的传奇Jeff，也就是大家口中的“姐夫”，宣布离职，出去创业。
姐夫是1999年加入谷歌的，那时候谷歌还是个小公司。
后来撑起整个谷歌的那些底层技术，MapReduce、BigTable、Spanner，都有他的名字，基本是他跟老搭档桑杰，两个人坐在一台电脑前结对写出来的。
2011年，他和吴恩达等人一起创立了Google Brain，后来又带队做出了TensorFlow。
再后来Google Brain和DeepMind合并，他当上了Google DeepMind的首席科学家，也是Gemini的技术负责人之一。
谷歌后来专门为他和桑杰两个人，设了一个新的最高职级，11级。
程序员圈子里甚至有个流传了快20年的梗，叫Jeff Dean Facts，专门编段子吹他。
比如：“编译器从来不给Jeff报警告，是Jeff给编译器报警告。”、“光在真空里的速度原来只有每小时35英里，后来Jeff Dean花了一个周末，优化了一下物理学。”之类的。。。
就是这么一个神一样的人，走了。
跟他一起走的，还有桑杰。
两天后，SemiAnalysis直接发了一篇文章，标题叫：
Gemini is Cooked but GCP is Cooking。
翻译过来就是，Gemini凉透了，但谷歌云正在起飞。
因为谷歌把大把的TPU算力，卖给了Anthropic这些对手，自家模型拉完了，但是卖铲子的生意反而越做越大。
这大半年里，谷歌基本就是靠Flash系列在续命，从3.5 Flash一路发到9月2号的3.8 Flash，这大概就是OpenAI再也掏不出来Astra了，天天发Luna，Anthropic也做不出来Fable了，天天发Haiku。
你就说魔幻不魔幻吧。。。
所以Argon对谷歌来说，真的不是一次普通的模型发布。
这是谷歌的，背水一战。
二. 基本信息
惯例先总结一下基本信息。
目前Gemini 4 Argon已经上线，20刀的Pro会员可以在Gemini APP里面用。
但是呢，如果你想在Antigravity（也就是Google家的Claude Code、Codex）里面去用，你必须要开100刀的Ultra会员才能用。
这一点非常的蛋疼。。。
然后，果不其然的就被喷了。
推理强度有三档，低中高，虽然他们这个翻译让我觉得团队里没有任何一个懂中文的人了。
模型上，Gemini一贯的传统，是个多模态的模型，支持视频、声音、图片、文字等几乎全模态的输入。
知识截止日期是2026年3月，比GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5都要旧一点。
上下文这块，有个小细节。
9月30号官宣的时候，谷歌的说法是，输出上限从上一代的6.4万Token，直接拉到100万。
但是今天的说法，变成了“输入输出合计100万”，也就是你的输入、思考、输出共享了，还配了一个所谓的续写协议，continuation protocol。
这玩意的意思就是，Argon一次请求，最多还是只能吐6.4万Token左右，跟上一代差不多，写到上限了，它不会直接断掉，会返回一个加密的续写令牌，里面记着它前面写到了哪，然后开发者再拿着这个令牌，把原来的请求原封不动再发一遍，它就接着往下写。
就这么一段一段接下去，最多能接到100万。。。
GPT-6 Astra原生单次最高输出甚至是128K，比Gemini 4 Argon还高点。。。
然后是价格。
现在是优惠期，2美刀/输入、10美刀/输出，跟GPT-6.1 Sol、Claude Sonnet 5.5，是同一个价。
但是优惠期是11月30号到期，优惠期一过，就变成4美刀/输入、20美刀/输出，就跟Claude Opus 5.5一模一样了。
但是对Agent来说，真正的大头，其实是缓存，对比一下。
Gemini 4 Argon，优惠期0.1美元，12月1号以后0.2美元。
GPT-6.1 Sol，0.1美元。
Claude Sonnet 5.5，0.1美元，这个是10月7号刚从0.2美元降下来的。
Claude Opus 5.5，0.2美元。
GPT-6 Astra，1美元。

Character.ai's Bankruptcy Documents Show the Economics of AI Don't Work
Jason Koebler
· Oct 13, 2026
at 4:06 PM
Character.ai enshittified its product but was still burning tons of cash, its bankruptcy documents say.
Character.ai’s bankruptcy is the one of the first dominos to fall in the long-foreseen AI bubble. The circumstances of its bankruptcy are exactly what critics of AI have been saying would happen : Character.ai lit a huge amount of money on fire running its product, did not bring in a lot of revenue, and faced enormous legal fees after causing harm to its users. Enshittifying its product to try to make its expenses cheaper did not work, according to a narrative filed in bankruptcy court Tuesday.
Disney has reportedly offered Character.ai $20 million to license some of its intellectual property; Last year, Disney sent Character.ai a cease and desist letter demanding it stop using its copyrighted characters without permission. In 2023, it was valued at $1 billion after raising $150 million in a round led by a16z.
Character.ai is one of the best-known AI chatbot companies that has become popular in the AI companion space. The company has faced various legal problems after being sued by the family of one of its users who killed himself after chatting with a Character.ai chatbot, and has been the target of regulators pushing for age verification tech because of its popularity with kids. In its bankruptcy filings, the company says that its enormous legal costs contributed to its bankruptcy, but that even without the legal problems, its business was wildly unsustainable.
An affidavit filed in bankruptcy court by Character.ai CEO Colin Adams noted simply: “Character’s impressive technology is expensive to operate,” and “at all times, Character has struggled with profitability and its operational expenditure has been high.”
The company said that in 2024, the company spent $13.8 million per month on AI compute; in 2025, it spent $10 million per month on AI compute. The company’s subscription revenue peaked at $2.8 million per month, but at times was less than $1 million per month. Its revenue from all sources, including ads, has peaked at $5.3 million per month.
The company spent $56.1 million on compute costs between January and August of 2026 alone and as of August was losing “approximately $8-9 million per month,” which it said was a massive improvement over the previous year. The company spent $19.7 million on employee salaries and benefits during that same eight-month time period and that a lot of employees quit because they “began questioning Character’s long-term viability,” according to the company.
Character said that its finances had improved to only be losing $8-9 million per month by taking “significant actions to reduce operational costs and improve revenues” by spending less on compute by simplifying its AI model, laying off staff, and injecting ads into its chats.
In May, 404 Media wrote that Character.ai’s changes are “what AI enshittification looks like,” with tons of ads, usage limits, guardrails, and “lobotomized” models. In the bankruptcy filing, Adams essentially admits that this enshittification was the strategy: “Character has, however, taken significant steps to reduce its operating burn, including transitioning inference workloads to lower-cost GPU capacity and post-training open-weight models rather than developing proprietary foundation models. At the same time, Character reduced its employee headcount,” he wrote. “In mid-2025, Character launched in-app advertising […] in early 2026, Character also introduced in-app purchases.”
While the lawsuits against Character are significant, they are also not unusual for an AI industry that has been plagued with legal problems relating to the theft of intellectual property and suggesting self harm or violence to their users. In other words, there is nothing in Character’s bankruptcy filings that could not be said about many other AI companies that are spending a huge amount of money on compute without having a revenue model that can support it. The difference between Character AI and behemoths like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Google is that those other companies have been able to repeatedly get injections of new cash, or, in the case of Meta and Google, have been able to subsidize their AI products with revenue from their massive advertising businesses.
The company said in a blog post that it will continue operating through the bankruptcy process: “The Character.ai platform remains up and running, and you can continue to access all services at this time. We're focused on finding the best path forward for our platform and community.”
As frontier models from the big players get better and have fewer guardrails, they will also likely continue to eat into the user base of more specialized products like Character.ai. Much of what you can do on Character.ai you can also do on ChatGPT or with Meta’s Muse, for example. It’s not clear whether AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic, or the AI industry in general have gotten too big or too important to fail, but Character’s bankruptcy shows that the runway for second-tier players is over.
About the author
Jason is a cofounder of 404 Media. He was previously the editor-in-chief of Motherboard. He loves the Freedom of Information Act and surfing.

items.title: ComfyUI 上线 NVIDIA VFX 节点，支持视频超分、补帧与 SDR 转 HDR
items.title_en: Nvidia VFX Nodes for Video Upscaling, Frame Generation and SDR-to-HDR, for VFX Professionals
items.summary: NVIDIA 的 RTX 视频特效模型以自定义节点形式登陆 ComfyUI，模型随节点分发并在本地 RTX GPU 上运行。
items.fullContent:
Releasing Nvidia VFX Nodes for Video Upscaling, Frame Generation and SDR-to-HDR, for VFX Professionals
ComfyUI Newsletter
Subscribe Sign in
Translate
Nvidia VFX Nodes for Video Upscaling, Frame Generation and SDR-to-HDR, for VFX Professionals
Upscale, interpolate, and convert to HDR locally on your RTX GPU, with better EXR support and color management built for VFX pipelines.
Rob and Alexis Rolland
Oct 13, 2026
4
3
Share
Nvidia’s RTX video effects now run inside ComfyUI as custom nodes . The models are fast, lightweight, ship with the nodes, and run locally on your Nvidia RTX GPU.
Nodes & Models Highlight
The RTX Video Super Resolution node upscales images and video frames up to 4×, either by a multiplier or to target dimensions up to 8192 px. The same node can also denoise or deblur a source without changing its resolution.
The RTX Video Frame Generation node creates new frames between adjacent pairs, for frame-rate conversion or slow motion. It works at 2× to 16× or at a specific timestep.
The RTX Video HDR node converts SDR images to BT.2020 HDR data, with HLG or PQ output. Contrast, saturation, middle gray, and peak luminance from 400 to 2000 nits are all adjustable, and a debanding pass is on by default.
Full workflow, optimal sequence is Super Resolution → Frame Generation → HDR
With the NVIDIA VFX Nodes, you can now run a full professional grade VFX pipeline end-to-end. Chaining the nodes from Video Super Resolution → Frame Generation → Video HDR is a quick and simple way to level up your footage and prepare it for the rest of your VFX pipeline.
The RTX Video Super Resolution node is a great option for efficient upscaling and has 19 modes that can handle different kinds of source material.
Standard modes upscale typical compressed footage.
High-bitrate modes upscale clean or lossless sources without unnecessary artifact suppression.
Streaming modes are tuned for broadcast and webcam streams.
Denoise and deblur modes clean up noise, compression artifacts, or softness and keep the input resolution.
A plain bicubic mode is also available when you don’t need AI processing.
Most modes run from LOW to ULTRA , trading speed for detail. An optional 10-bit encoding preserves more precision. The frame count and frame rate are unchanged, which sets your footage up for the next step in the workflow.
The RTX Video Frame Generation node offers two ways to generate new frames within an input video. Frame-rate multiplier mode fills every gap evenly, from 2× to 16×. To keep the original duration, encode the output at the source frame rate times the multiplier. Specific-timestep mode inserts one frame per pair at any point between the two frames, which suits custom timing in downstream workflows. The Quality parameter runs from LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH . Shot changes are detected automatically, and a manual option marks a known cut. Like RTX Video Super Resolution, the node offers an optional 10-bit encoding for more precision.
In the final step of the workflow, use the RTX Video HDR node to convert SDR images to BT.2020 HDR at their original dimensions. You can tune the conversion with three tone controls. The Contrast and saturation parameters work as they do in any grade. Middle gray sets the reference level for midtones, which decides how bright the overall image sits. Peak luminance tells the node how bright the brightest highlights should get. Set it to match the display you’re grading for, anywhere from 400 to 2000 nits. A debanding pass is on by default, which helps smooth out the visible steps that can show up in gradients like skies when SDR footage is stretched to a wider range. The output is a standard ComfyUI image with no color-space metadata, so downstream Create Video nodes need to be told whether the data is HDR or HDR PQ. The color management and EXR support in this release also handle that step.
Finally, the node pack’s example_workflows folder has a starter workflow for each node: image upscaling, video upscaling, frame generation, and HDR conversion, plus one for converting longer videos to HDR using the loop nodes. To see all three nodes working together, try the full VFX pipeline below.
Nvidia VFX Nodes Workflow
Better EXR support for VFX pipelines
In addition to Nvidia’s VFX nodes, we’re improving support for EXR files format. EXR is the standard format in VFX pipelines, and this release makes it much easier to work with in ComfyUI.
The Save Image (Advanced) node can now write half-float (16-bit) EXRs, now the default, as well as full-float (32-bit) EXRs.
The Load Image node has been improved to ensure images remain intact. It now reads half-float and full-float EXRs. Superwhites above 1.0 and negative values come through untouched instead of being silently clipped, so the full range of data is preserved.
Color management gets an upgrade as well. The Convert Image Color Space node handles sRGB, scene-linear Rec.709, HDR HLG and PQ (Rec.2020), ARRI LogC3 (EI 800) and ACEScct.
Convert Image Color Space node, EXR preview in Load Image and Save Image (Advanced) nodes.
Preview & Download EXRs
EXRs also get a major quality-of-life improvement: they are now easier to inspect and to download. Since web browsers can’t display EXR files, our new asset management system attaches a JPEG preview to every EXR output. The preview is visible in the save and load nodes, in the Assets panel, and in the Jobs history. The small sun button in the load and save nodes also opens the EXR file in the HDR Viewer for more comfortable viewing.
Remark: Previews are only available when ComfyUI starts with the command line argument --enable-asset . The flag is set by default in Comfy Desktop since version 1.1.7 and in ComfyUI portable since 0.40.0 .
Finally, when a save node outputs a sequence of images, the new Download images action lets you pick frames, or hit “Download all”, and download them as a single zip.

items.summary: Apple 发布配备 7 英寸 Liquid Retina 显示屏的 HomeView，集娱乐、FaceTime、家庭监控和语音自动化于一体，标准版与壁挂版均定价 299 美元，11 月 13 日起在美英加澳等市场发售。
items.fullContent:
Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment and manage the home - Apple
0 +
opens in new window PRESS RELEASE October 13, 2026
Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home
Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core
Powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, Apple HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place.
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView , designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core. 1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2
Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13.
“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”
HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
Elegantly Designed for Any Space
HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable.
HomeView is available in four beautiful colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
A Liquid Retina display connected to a domed base by a stainless steel hinge provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height.
HomeView comes with a color-matched USB-C cable.
The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer.
A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation.
Available in space gray and silver, the wall-mounted HomeView can be attached using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, extending the experience to more places.
A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home
HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests.
HomeView can recognize up to six users by their face, and each user can personalize their Home Screen apps and widgets.
Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence
HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable and conversational.
With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.
With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery.
With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information by drawing on each user’s personal context.
Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, so users can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.
With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant.
Faces for Every Style
Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments.
Users can customize HomeView with a collection of playful faces that display useful information at a glance, taking full advantage of the Liquid Retina display.
Rich Entertainment Anywhere in the Home
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts, Apple News, 4 Apple TV, and compatible third-party audio and video apps. 5 With Handoff, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.
HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Podcasts and Apple Music.
Connecting Users to What Matters Most
HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking.
HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods charging case, or personal item with an AirTag attached. And with Live Activities, HomeView surfaces timely, at-a-glance information, like the song that’s currently playing, an active timer, or an incoming Intercom message from another room.
The Ultimate Smart Home Dashboard
HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds. The Home Modular face offers instant access to users’ favorite accessories, while the Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds at once, letting users keep an eye on doorstep deliveries and pets playing in the yard.
With HomeView, users can securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice by using Siri AI.
With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door. With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it. 7 Offering added peace of mind, HomeView also detects the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and alerts users on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.
HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories. 8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more. 9
HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — Apple’s first lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
Private and Secure by Design
Like every Apple product, HomeView was built with privacy and security at its core. HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system. Isolation features added across many core components of the silicon work in tandem to protect Secure Exclaves and keep them segregated from the rest of the system. Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple. To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. 10
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud. When processed in Private Cloud Compute, data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.
Apple HomeView and the Environment
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 11 and designed to be recycled.
Pricing and Availability
Customers in Australia , Canada , India , New Zealand , the UK , and the U.S. can pre-order Apple HomeView in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray for $299 (U.S.), and Apple HomeView (Wall Mounted) in space gray and silver for $299 (U.S.), starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app. Customers in Singapore can pre-order starting Thursday, October 15, at 9 a.m. SGT. Both models will be available in these countries beginning Friday, November 13. Customers in South Africa will be able to pre-order Apple HomeView and Apple HomeView (Wall Mounted) through Apple Authorized Resellers, with availability beginning Friday, November 13. Apple HomeView is not available for sale in the European Union, as Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU. Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home. Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app. Power Mount PoE Wired will be available starting in early 2027 for $129.95 (U.S.).
Siri AI on HomeView is available in English in the U.S., Australia , Canada , India , New Zealand , Singapore , South Africa , and the UK.
Canadian French-language support will be offered later via a free software update.

Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home
Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView , designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core. 1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2
Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13.
“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”
Elegantly Designed for Any Space
HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable.
The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer.
A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation.
A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home
HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests.
Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence
HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.

Search agent traces by behavior with AI Search in LangSmith
Arjun Natarajan
Eugene Yurtsev
Suraj Vathsa
October 13, 2026
7
min
Go back to blog
Create agents
Create agents
Share
Key Takeaways
AI Search now enables users to find conversations based on semantic understanding of traces, like "did the user get frustrated?" or "did PII leak?"
Describe a behavior in plain language, and a fast decision model reads traces and returns the ones where it happened.
LangSmith uses trajectories to normalize traces, reduce context bloat, and deliver query results fast.
Agent traces are large, multimodal, and information-dense. They capture key details such as user inputs, how agents respond, and logic failures. That makes traces uniquely valuable for understanding user behavior and improving agent performance, but traditional data platforms weren’t built for large, unstructured payloads like this.
To make trace data useful, teams need infrastructure that can support the full lifecycle: ingest and store high-volume runs, query traces flexibly, and turn them into views for debugging, product analysis, and operational workflows like annotations. That’s why we built SmithDB, the database purpose-built for trace data in LangSmith , and more recently Custom Apps , which let teams create tailored views on top of their traces.
Today, we’re adding AI Search , a new way to query traces using natural language.
Why we built AI Search
Each trace contains user inputs, agent reasoning, tool calls, and responses, all the information required to understand where agents are performing well and where they fail. Teams using LangSmith often mine their agent traces to discover examples for an eval dataset or conversations for a reviewer in an annotation queue .
However, discovering the right traces can be cumbersome. Questions like "did PII leak?" or "did the user get frustrated?" don't map cleanly to a single trace attribute like tags or metadata, and cannot be answered by full-text search either. They require an understanding of the trace contents. Until now, that meant setting up an evaluator ahead of time or going through traces manually.
That's why we built AI Search. You describe the behavior you're looking for, and LangSmith returns the traces where it happened. This enables you to find needle-in-haystack traces and search for troublesome patterns ad hoc.
What you can search for
You can search for anything that shows up in the content of a trace. You might look for an agent that said it finished a task but didn't, a user who seemed frustrated or pushed back on an answer, a request to a model that leaked PII, or someone trying to cancel their subscription. Product teams can search for "requests for integrations we don't support", "competitor mentioned", or "users confused about onboarding" and see where the product falls short, in users' own words.
AI Search also works alongside the filters you already use, so a search can run only on traces that errored, or only with a specific tag.
How we built it
Why a model reads every trace
Vector search is the usual way to search by meaning instead of exact words. It turns your query and each trace into an embedding, a short list of numbers that captures what the text is about. Then it returns the traces whose embeddings are closest to your query's. That works well for topic search, like finding conversations about billing. But an embedding packs a whole trace into one small vector, and that compression is lossy. Important details related to your query can get lost. A trace where the agent did the work successfully and one where it only said it did can end up with nearly the same embedding. Telling them apart takes a model that reads the actual words of the trace along with your question, so it can reason about what happened.
Until recently, doing that at search time was too slow and too expensive. Fast decision models changed that. They answer one narrow question about an input quickly and cheaply enough to run at scale. AI Search pairs decision model inference with SmithDB , our data layer for agent observability. As traces arrive, SmithDB turns them into trajectories. When you run a search, your filters narrow the candidates, and the decision model checks each remaining trajectory against your description.
Traces are large and come in many formats
Traces come from many sources: the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, LangChain, LangGraph, the Vercel AI SDK, OpenTelemetry, and more. Each records messages a little differently. Traces also repeat themselves. Agents often re-send the conversation history with every LLM call, so the first message shows up again in every call after it.
SmithDB turns these traces into a trajectory for each session. A trajectory is a distilled view of the agent's work: each message, tool call, and tool result, listed once. SmithDB builds it as traces arrive and puts every supported format into the same shape.
AI Search analyzes trajectories instead of raw traces. Because every format has the same trajectory shape, one search works across agents built on different SDKs. Removing the repeat messages reduces context bloat, so searches run faster. A trajectory also covers the whole session, so if you search for "the user tried to cancel", the model sees what the user asked, what the agent did, and how the conversation ended.
Each LLM call re-sends the whole history. The trajectory view shows the session once. Trajectories are still long
Removing duplicates helps, but agent trajectories are still long. To get a sense of how long, we sampled 150 random conversations from Open SWE , the open source coding agent the LangChain team uses every day. Each task runs in its own sandbox with shell access and can hand work off to subagents, so the conversations get big.
A couple of them ran past a million tokens, even in a sample this small. Searching for a rare behavior means reading through a lot of conversations, so AI Search regularly runs into ones that size and can't read every token.
Most questions don't need all of those tokens, though. Many questions are about what the user asked and how the agent replied. In the median conversation, about 2K of its 72K tokens came from the user's messages and the agent's replies. About 85% was tool output, mostly file reads and shell commands.
💡 Even when a trace runs past a million tokens, many questions about agent behavior can be answered with a few thousand.
‍
Each trajectory gets a fixed token budget, filled in priority order. User messages and the agent's replies to the user go in first. The rest of the budget goes to everything else: intermediate AI messages (the agent's reasoning and tool calls), tool results, and system messages. If the next message only partly fits, it's trimmed to fill the budget, and anything after it is dropped.
AI Search fills an 8K token budget in priority order, then sends the kept messages to the decision model in their original order. Searches have to stay fast at scale
SmithDB is built to ingest and scan large volumes of agent trace data. When you run a search, your structured filters narrow the candidates first. The decision model then checks each remaining trajectory against your description, many in parallel. While the model checks one batch of trajectories, SmithDB is already fetching and preparing the next batch. Matches are streamed back as they're found, so you don't wait for the full scan.
Structured filters narrow the candidates, the model checks each trajectory, and matches stream out as they're found. What's next
We're still learning which questions people ask most. The hardest conversations to classify are the ones with subtle differences. Telling "the user gave up" apart from "the user got what they needed and left" can come down to a couple of turns in a long trajectory. We want to see whether a model tuned on traces tells them apart more reliably.
The token budget works well when the answer is found in what the user and agent said. Other questions need different evidence. An agent ignoring a tool error only shows up in the tool results. We're exploring ways to pick context based on the question, and signals that show when the model is unsure, so it can take a second pass with more context.
We'd also like to go past a plain list of matches by grouping similar results or summarizing what they have in common.
Get started
AI Search is in public beta on LangSmith Cloud in the GCP US, EU, and APAC regions, at no additional cost. Org admins can turn it on in settings, and it then shows up on the tracing page. The AI Search docs have the details. Let us know what you search for.
‍

Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
Ivan Mehta
5:23 AM PDT · October 13, 2026
Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document , the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
“Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the board determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders,” Character.AI CEO Colin Adams said in a statement.
The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.
The company said Disney will provide transition services via former Character.AI employees who joined the entertainment giant last month alongside its former CEO Karandeep Singh Anand .
Adams said the company would continue operating during the sale process, which is expected to close in late November or early December. However, he did note that there isn’t yet a bid for the company’s assets or a buyer.
“We hope that the sale process will yield an actionable proposal that will allow continued operations of the Character.ai platform. If such a bid is unavailable, however, the platform will be wound down,” Adams wrote.
Character.AI has had a tumultuous five years. Founded by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper, and Daniel De Freitas in late 2021, the startup initially focused on training foundation models and developing an AI chatbot platform that lets people create custom characters they could chat with.
By September 2022, the startup reached unicorn valuation with a $150 million fundraise on the back of high demand for its platform, with the company saying at the time that its users had exchanged more than 2 billion messages with its bots in five months, and active users were averaging more than two hours on the platform daily.
In May 2023, the Character.AI’s apps attracted more than 1.7 million installs in their first week after launch. But about a year later, in August 2024, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license the startup’s models, and both Shazeer and De Freitas returned to the search giant . At that time, the startup’s general counsel, Dominic Perella, stepped in as interim CEO, and the company moved away from training foundation models to focus on growth.
Character.AI’s traction didn’t slow, however, with its platform recording 20 million monthly active users by October of that year.
But things got difficult after the startup was sued following the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot on its platform. Soon after, Texas launched an investigation to assess if the platform conformed to child privacy and safety laws. The company subsequently settled some of these lawsuits , added more safety features, and banned minors from its platform.
In June of last year, the company appointed Anand, a former Brex and Meta executive, as CEO, and expanded its products to add AI video generation, and social feeds. The company has since tried to introduce new ways to spur user engagement via interactive storytelling formats as well as microdramas.
But the fact that the company had to file for bankruptcy shows that such changes couldn’t move the needle on sustainability for the startup.
It also shows that consumer-facing AI products are really hard to scale and monetize. Character.AI was one of the top apps in terms of time spent, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. But high engagement can be a double-edged sword; AI costs rise the more people use the app, which consequently also increases the pressure to monetize users.
Image Credits: Sensor Tower Character.AI has raised over $193 million in funding across multiple rounds from investors including Lightspeed, SV Angel, Greycroft, and a16z, according to PitchBook.

items.title_en: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
items.summary: NVIDIA 介绍 RTX Spark 平台生态就绪情况，RTX Spark 笔记本将于 10 月 16 日（周五）上市，搭载最高 128GB 统一内存和 1 petaflop AI 算力。
items.fullContent:
All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark | NVIDIA Blog Skip to content
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.
Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16 . Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark.
New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include:
New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark: Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.
The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15.
NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.
Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark: Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more.
The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app.
NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows.
NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport.
Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark: Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries.
GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark.
Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app.
Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus: A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta .
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23.
The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23.
Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools
AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year.
From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents.
Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark
From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app.
These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC.
After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks.
Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions.
Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills .
NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant.
Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark.
This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint.
Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw.
Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents.
The Perfect PAIR
Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR , a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems.
The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements.
PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release.
Sparking Creativity
RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance.
Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark
Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows.
In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects.
The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds.
Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content
Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles.
A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app.
RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI
ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/comfyui_nvidia_vfx_nodes_explainer_4k48_v4.mp4
RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow.
For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading.
Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction
Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access.
Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time.
Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark
Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype.
RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud.
Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready
NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing:
The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm.
The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15.
The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages.
97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels.
Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA.
Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI
In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence.
Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally , and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations.
Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches.
Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App
Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs.
Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows , a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog .
Llama Windows runs from the Windows 11 system tray, with local models and recommended models from the Hugging Face Hub one click away. Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5
RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant , Cyberpunk 2077 , Fortnite , Gears of War: E-Day , Genshin Impact , Hogwarts Legacy , Honkai: Star Rail , Marvel Rivals , NARAKA: BLADEPOINT , NBA 2K27 , World of Warcraft and many more.
NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark .
DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November.
DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX .
Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com.
Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG , allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.

Key Takeaways
Building long-running agents takes constant context management, and making those decisions with a frontier LLM is slow and expensive. ScaleDown’s constrained decoding models (CDMs) make them faster and cheaper.
langchain-scaledown makes it easy to use ScaleDown models in your agent, and ships with middleware for summarization, tool result compression, and extraction.
ScaleDown is now supported in the LangSmith LLM Gateway, so its calls are traced and count toward your spend and rate limits.
Building long-running agents comes down to the art of context management: deciding which information goes into the context window, and when. That means summarizing old history, compacting large tool results, and extracting the right data from long inputs. Each of those steps is a decision. Historically we’ve made them with LLMs, which is slow and expensive at the volume a long-running agent needs.
To make those decisions faster and cheaper, we now have a langchain-scaledown integration and support in the LangSmith LLM Gateway for ScaleDown ’s constrained decoding models (CDMs). Where a general-purpose LLM writes any string one token at a time, a CDM is trained for one task and only returns answers that task allows, like a label from your list or spans of the input. That lets it be much smaller, faster, and cheaper: ScaleDown reports its models are 200x faster and 467x cheaper than frontier models on these narrow tasks.
The integration ships with three middlewares for LangChain and Deep Agents : one summarizes old history, one compresses large tool results, and one extracts structured data from the conversation. In this post, we cover what ScaleDown’s models are and how to use them to scale down your agent’s context.
What models does ScaleDown offer?
ScaleDown has four models, each trained for a single task, so each can be far more efficient than a general-purpose LLM:
Summarize writes a short summary of long text.
Compress cuts a block of context down to the parts relevant to a question.
Extract pulls the fields you describe out of text, each with a confidence score and its position in the source.
Classify scores text against labels you define and returns a probability for each. You can decide whether to return a natural language reason for why the classification was made.
The agent model runs the loop, and ScaleDown handles the context work around it: Summarize before each model call, Classify on the model’s output, Compress on tool results, and Extract on the user’s message. Every model takes up to 1M tokens of input, so a full contract, a long policy page, or an hour of agent history fits in one call with no chunking. They’re also multimodal : Extract, Summarize, and Classify take images and scanned PDFs directly in addition to unstructured text, so a screenshot or a scanned invoice works as an input.
On ScaleDown's own benchmarks , measured against the average of GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 Mini, and GPT-5.4 Nano on public datasets , Summarize is 41x cheaper and 2.7x faster, and Compress is 138x cheaper and 1.8x faster, while scoring higher on accuracy for both.
If you’ve used a decision model like Jev , ScaleDown Classify will feel familiar: both return a typed answer with a probability. Jev takes text only, up to 32K tokens of state per question. Classify takes up to 1M tokens, images included, and adds a one-sentence reason to each decision. When an agent routes a ticket or stops a run based on a label, the reason tells you why, which makes the agent easier to debug.
Summarizing message history
Long-running agents need summarization because their history eventually outgrows the context window. A coding agent that has been working for an hour has dozens of file reads and tool outputs in its history, most of which it no longer needs verbatim. Summarizing them with another frontier model call adds cost and latency every time the history fills up.
Once history crosses the trigger, ScaleDown replaces the older messages with one summary and the recent messages stay as is. ScaledownSummarizationMiddleware replaces Deep Agents’ built-in summarization middleware . It takes the same trigger and keep options to decide when to summarize and which recent messages to keep, and ScaleDown writes the summary:
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from langchain_scaledown import ScaledownSummarizationMiddleware
agent = create_deep_agent(
model="openai:gpt-6-sol",
tools=[run_tests],
middleware=[
ScaledownSummarizationMiddleware(
"openai:gpt-6-sol", # the agent’s model, used for its context window
trigger=("fraction", 0.8),
keep=("fraction", 0.1),
),
],
) The agent keeps its own model for planning and writing code. Only the summary moves to ScaleDown, which by default returns the same sections as LangChain’s summary prompt (intent, summary, artifacts, and next steps). If a ScaleDown call fails, the middleware leaves history as is and the agent keeps running. The same middleware works with LangChain’s create_agent .
Compressing tool results
Long-running agents call a lot of tools, and every large result stays in context for the rest of the run. A fetched web page can run to tens of thousands of characters when the agent only needs one paragraph of it. Every later step pays for those tokens again, and the agent gets worse at staying on task as its context fills up.
The model asks for what it needs on the tool call, and ScaleDown cuts the tool result down to the relevant parts before the model sees it. ScaledownToolCompressionMiddleware adds an optional compression_query parameter to your tools. When the model only needs part of a result, it fills in compression_query on the tool call, for example "refund policy for EU orders" . The middleware strips it before the tool runs, then ScaleDown compresses the output to the relevant parts before the model sees it:
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from langchain_scaledown import ScaledownToolCompressionMiddleware
agent = create_deep_agent(
model="openai:gpt-6-luna",
tools=[search_docs, fetch_url],
middleware=[ScaledownToolCompressionMiddleware(tools=["fetch_url"])],
) Your tools don’t change, so this works with any tool, including MCP tools . In this trace , ScaleDown cut a long docs page by almost 90% before the model saw it. The compressed result starts with a note like this one, so the model can call the tool again without compression_query if it needs the full page:
[Compressed by ScaleDown for "refund policy for EU orders":
18,402 -> 3,110 chars.
Call this tool again without `compression_query` for the full output.] Extracting structured data
Agents constantly pull specific values out of what they read, like an ID, a date, or a field the next tool call needs. That extraction sits inside the agent loop, so it has to be fast enough not to add latency to every turn, and exact enough that a tool can use the value as is.
For example, before a support agent can file a ticket, it needs the order number, the error message, and the customer’s email. The main model could fill those in as tool arguments, but it may paraphrase an error code or mistype an email address instead of copying it exactly.
ScaledownExtractionMiddleware hands this step to ScaleDown. You describe each field in plain language, and Extract copies the value from the text. A field can also be a set of labels, which ScaleDown answers with Classify, so the ticket can be routed by issue type. Before the first model call of a run, the middleware sends the user’s messages to Extract and saves the fields to agent state under scaledown_extraction , where your tools can read them:
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from langchain.tools import ToolRuntime, tool

items.title: Liquid AI 发布 LFM2.5-24B-A2B 端侧推理模型
items.title_en: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents
items.source: Liquid AI 模型与工程博客（网页）
items.summary: Liquid AI 发布开源权重模型 LFM2.5-24B-A2B，总参数 24B、每 token 激活 2B，定位端侧快速智能体。
items.fullContent:
LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents | Blog | Liquid AI
Try our API
Today, we release LFM2.5-24B-A2B , a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It is the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family, which now spans two orders of magnitude: from LFM2.5-230M to LFM2.5-24B-A2B .
LFM2.5-24B-A2B is competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, on five of eight agentic and tool-use benchmarks, scoring 48.09 on LiveClaw versus 38.19 and 27.69 on AutomationBench versus 8.72.  Because only 2B parameters are active per token, it runs up to 1.7× faster than comparable MoEs on-device, with 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max and up to 21K output tokens/s on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU.
The base (LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base) and post-trained (LFM2.5-24B-A2B) models are open-weight and available today on Hugging Face and our Playground . Check out our docs on how to run and fine-tune it locally.
What changed since LFM2-24B-A2B
LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on our previous LFM2-24B-A2B release, with an expanded vocabulary and context window, scaled-up pretraining, and large-scale reinforcement learning. Unlike its predecessor, LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer. We adopted this strategy to leverage its high decode speed and improve answer quality.
Architecture. It keeps the 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The two architectural changes are the context window extension from 32,768 to 131,072 tokens, and the in-place tokenizer expansion , which doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization.
Pre-training was scaled up from 17T tokens to 33T tokens.
Mid-training has two phases. The first runs 2T tokens at 32K context on curated, higher-quality data weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text. The second runs 300B tokens at 131K context, weighted toward long context data. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear throughout both phases to prepare the model for agentic workloads.
Post-training turns LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base into the agentic LFM2.5-24B-A2B in a five-stage pipeline as illustrated below: (1) Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), (2) Teacher Specialization, (3) non-agentic and (4) agentic Multi-Domain On-Policy Distillation (MOPD), and (5) Agentic Reinforcement Learning (Agentic RL), training the model inside agent harnesses, such as OpenClaw , Hermes Agent , Pi , and OpenCode . Figure 2: LFM2.5-24B-A2B Post-training recipe
During teacher specialization, LFM2.5-24B-A2B exhibited well-known reward-hacking behaviors: searching for the final answer in a repository's git history or on platforms like GitHub, PyPI, and Hugging Face. More surprisingly, it even figured out it was in a sandbox, as shown in the examples below.
This behavior looks emergent but might be explained by training data containing similar patterns. We tightened our sandboxes in response, and all reported results below come from sealed evaluation environments.
Benchmarks
We evaluated LFM2.5-24B-A2B across 16 benchmarks covering tool use and agentic workflows, knowledge, instruction following, math, and coding. Despite being the smallest model in total and active number of parameters, it is competitive with, and often outperforms, larger MoEs with ~50% more total and active parameters, such as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.

items.title_en: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
